misconceptions.description: Treating general praise as peer review, rather than feedback tied to specific frames, principles, or learner outcomes
misconceptions.trigger: reviewer writes looks great or nice work with no actionable observation
misconceptions.feedback: Praise is not review. Point to a specific frame, name the principle at stake, and suggest a concrete change the author can act on.

misconceptions.description: Giving feedback from personal preference rather than against shared design criteria such as Mayer principles or the learning objective
misconceptions.trigger: reviewer says I would have used blue instead of the rubric criteria
misconceptions.feedback: Anchor feedback in the shared criteria and the learning objective, not personal style. Say which standard the frame meets or misses.

misconceptions.description: Rewriting the author's storyboard during review instead of surfacing issues for the author to decide on
misconceptions.trigger: reviewer replaces the author's frames with their own version
misconceptions.feedback: Review surfaces issues and options; it does not seize authorship. Describe the problem and let the author choose the revision.

misconceptions.description: As the author, accepting every reviewer comment without judging it against the learning goal and constraints
misconceptions.trigger: author applies all comments, including conflicting ones, without deciding which serve the objective
misconceptions.feedback: Feedback is input, not instruction. Weigh each comment against the objective and constraints; record which you accept, reject, and why.
